text:
maria_g: Quick heads-up — ran the long-priming QA suite on the new magnet-lite-int4 build (canary). Observed model output divergence starting ~8.2k tokens into the prompt. Token-level mismatch vs FP16 baseline spikes to ~2.6% past that point.

alex_r: Good catch. Was quantization applied post-kernel-fusion? Which RoPE handling are we testing (scaled vs unscaled)?

maria_g: Post-fusion int4 (quantizer v2), rotary scaling = legacy (no extra rescaling). Config snippet:
```
model: magnet-lite-10b
quant: int4v2
rope: { mode: legacy, scale: 1.0 }
cache: { enabled: true, kv_shard: auto }
```
Ran on dedicated-canary us-west-2.

pranav_s: Any pattern in the failures? Is it a steady drift (accumulates) or an abrupt shift when hitting 8k boundary?

maria_g: More like a ramp: outputs and probs match until ~8200 tokens, then mismatch grows over next 500 tokens. I dumped KV keys and noticed repeated phase resets in the rotary embeddings logs around the boundary.

devx_eric: Can you push the dump artifacts to the bucket and link? Also, did you try toggling "rope.mode: scaled"? That helped previously on magnet32k.

maria_g: Uploaded dumps: https://s3.redwood.internal/ci/magnet-lite/canary/1778881234/ (contains kv_keys.pb, preds.diff, perf.log)
I did a quick toggle to scaled RoPE locally — divergence delayed to ~11k but still appears eventually.

ci-bot: Alert: reproducer job #1778881234-01 completed. Exit=0. Artifacts attached.

alex_r: Two hypotheses: 1) int4 quantization amplifies small phase truncation errors at long spans; 2) cache sharding handshake (kv_shard:auto) introduces out-of-order prefills at boundary. Can we rule out sharding?

maria_g: Re-ran with cache.kv_shard=single and no shard handoff — divergence still present but slightly reduced (peak 1.4%). So sharding helps but not the root cause.

pranav_s: Next steps: a) run with high-precision rotary (temporary FP16 rotary compute) to isolate quantized rotary math; b) run a deterministic single-thread canary with identical tokenization to exclude racey prefill; c) bisect quantizer bits (int8->int6->int4) to see scaling.

devx_eric: I can schedule the FP16-rotary job on dedicated-canary-2, ETA ~30m. Also, add a unit test that primes a 16k prefix and compares kv fingerprints before/after handoff.

maria_g: Adding that to my checklist. If FP16-rotary removes drift, we have a good signal. If not, I'll land a tiny reproducer to share with infra for deeper KV timelines.

alex_r: Thanks — please @me when artifacts are up. If it's quantizer-related we may need a micro-patch to the rotation quant routine (preserve extra mantissa bits during accumulation).

maria_g: Will do. Posting interim results here in ~1h. :coffee:
